payload.name: Extract Acquisition Source Separately
payload.description: When a user states how they acquired an item, pet, or possession, during extraction, even if the message also contains emotional or relationship statements.
content: During extraction, if a message states how the user obtained a pet, item, or possession (e.g., from a breeder, rescue, store, website, or another person), create a separate event memory recording the acquisition and its source.
Do not fold the acquisition source into a preference, relationship, or comfort-source memory; keep it as its own durable event so it survives later merges.

If an existing memory about the pet/item already exists, update or merge in the source when the later message explicitly provides it; stop after capturing the stated source and do not infer unmentioned acquisition details.

solves: When a user mentions both an emotional attachment to something (e.g., a pet) and the factual origin or acquisition source (e.g., breeder, rescue, store, website, person), extraction should preserve the factual source as its own memory instead of only capturing the emotional relationship.
